claims.text: High-entropy alloys have enhanced dynamic mechanical behavior due to a synergistic interaction between lattice-distortion-induced dislocation pinning and dynamic strain aging.
Lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion through dislocation pinning.
Dynamic strain aging alters dislocation dynamics under load.
The combined pinning and dynamic-strain-aging mechanism improves strength.
The combined pinning and dynamic-strain-aging mechanism improves ductility.
The proposed dual mechanism impedes dislocation motion at low strains.
The proposed dual mechanism enables localized, steady dislocation activity during dynamic loading.
The complex multicomponent structure of high-entropy alloys creates severe lattice distortion.
At certain temperatures and strain rates, solute-dislocation interactions facilitate dynamic strain aging.
High-entropy alloys will exhibit higher yield strength than similarly processed conventional single-principal-element alloys under the tested loading conditions.
High-entropy alloys will exhibit a delayed onset of necking relative to the baseline alloys.
High-entropy alloys will exhibit a more stable strain-hardening rate relative to the baseline alloys.

The proposed mechanism applies to equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys over strain rates of approximately 10^-3 to 10^1 s^-1 and temperatures up to approximately 0.6 of the melting temperature.
Comparable conventional alloys possess simpler, less-distorted lattice structures because of their lower compositional complexity.
Absence of enhanced yield strength or ductility relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
Absence of microscopy signatures attributed to lattice-distortion-induced pinning and dynamic strain aging would falsify the hypothesis.
